final_proof:
Let $\Z_p$ be the ring of $p$-adic integers, which is defined as the valuation ring of the $p$-adic field $\Q_p$:
$$ \Z_p = \{x \in \Q_p : 
orm{x}_p \le 1\} $$

Recall that a commutative ring is a local ring if and only if the set of its non-units forms an ideal. When this condition holds, that ideal of non-units is the unique maximal ideal of the ring.

Let $U$ denote the set of units (invertible elements) of $\Z_p$. Since the $p$-adic norm is multiplicative, for any $x, y \in \Z_p$ with $xy = 1$, we have $
orm{x}_p 
orm{y}_p = 
orm{1}_p = 1$. As $x, y \in \Z_p$, we have $
orm{x}_p \le 1$ and $
orm{y}_p \le 1$, which forces $
orm{x}_p = 
orm{y}_p = 1$. Conversely, if $x \in \Z_p$ and $
orm{x}_p = 1$, then its inverse $x^{-1} \in \Q_p$ satisfies $
orm{x^{-1}}_p = 
orm{x}_p^{-1} = 1 \le 1$, so $x^{-1} \in \Z_p$, meaning $x$ is a unit.
Thus, the group of units is $U = \{x \in \Q_p : 
orm{x}_p = 1\}$.

It follows that the set of non-units in $\Z_p$ is:
$$ M = \Z_p \setminus U = \{x \in \Q_p : 
orm{x}_p < 1\} $$
Since the possible non-zero values of the $p$-adic norm on $\Q_p$ are $p^k$ for $k \in \Z$, the strict inequality $
orm{x}_p < 1$ is equivalent to $
orm{x}_p \le p^{-1}$.

We claim that $M$ is precisely the principal ideal $p\Z_p$.
First, let $x \in p\Z_p$. Then $x = py$ for some $y \in \Z_p$. We have $
orm{x}_p = 
orm{p}_p 
orm{y}_p = p^{-1} 
orm{y}_p$. Since $
orm{y}_p \le 1$, we get $
orm{x}_p \le p^{-1} < 1$, so $x \in M$. Thus, $p\Z_p \subseteq M$.
Conversely, let $x \in M$. Then $
orm{x}_p \le p^{-1}$. We can write $x = p(x/p)$ in $\Q_p$. The norm of $x/p$ is $
orm{x/p}_p = 
orm{x}_p / 
orm{p}_p \le p^{-1} / p^{-1} = 1$. This implies that $x/p \in \Z_p$. Thus, $x = p(x/p) \in p\Z_p$. This shows that $M \subseteq p\Z_p$.
Therefore, $M = p\Z_p$.

Since the set of non-units $M$ is equal to the principal ideal generated by $p$ in $\Z_p$, it forms an ideal.
Hence, by the standard characterization of local rings, $\Z_p$ is a local ring, proving (a).
Furthermore, the ideal of non-units is exactly the unique maximal ideal of the ring, so $p\Z_p$ is the unique maximal ideal of $\Z_p$, proving (b). $ lacksquare$
